#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Nexus Code Security Lifecycle Gates (WP-11, INC-12, SCAN-001..SCAN-005, REL-001..REL-004)
# Enforces non-bypassable pre-commit, build, and release security gates.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ROOT_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"

echo "========================================================"
echo "  NEXUS CODE LIFECYCLE SECURITY SCANNING GATES (INC-12) "
echo "========================================================"

# SCAN-002 / SCAN-004: Non-bypassable check. Any attempt to bypass fails the gate.
if [[ -n "${SKIP_SECURITY_GATES:-}" && "${SKIP_SECURITY_GATES}" != "0" && "${SKIP_SECURITY_GATES}" != "false" ]]; then
  echo "[-] ERROR [SCAN-002]: Security gates are non-bypassable. SKIP_SECURITY_GATES is prohibited." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -n "${BYPASS_SECURITY_SCAN:-}" && "${BYPASS_SECURITY_SCAN}" != "0" && "${BYPASS_SECURITY_SCAN}" != "false" ]]; then
  echo "[-] ERROR [SCAN-002]: Security gates are non-bypassable. BYPASS_SECURITY_SCAN is prohibited." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Gate 1: Dependency Vulnerability Audit (SCAN-001, SCAN-004)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "[*] [Gate 1] Auditing Node.js dependencies via npm audit..."
cd "${ROOT_DIR}/cli"
# npm exports its configuration to child processes as npm_config_* variables. When this gate runs under
export PATH := $(HOME)/.cargo/bin:$(PATH)
APPROVED_RUST_BUILD_IMAGE := rust:1.95.0-bookworm@sha256:4c2fd73ef19c5ef9d54bee03b06b2839a392604fbfcd578ed948b71b37c1d7fb

.PHONY: all setup build build-core build-cli check clean test test-ci test-fixture-notice audit security-scan sbom verify-reproducibility

all: build

setup:
	npm --prefix cli install
	cargo build --release --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml
	npm --prefix cli run build

build: build-core build-cli

build-core:
	cargo build --release --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml

build-cli:
	npm --prefix cli run build

check:
	node cli/dist/index.js check

clean:
	cargo clean --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml
	rm -rf dist cli/dist cli/node_modules

audit:
	npm --prefix cli audit

security-scan:
	bash scripts/security_gates.sh

sbom:
	bash scripts/generate_sbom.sh

verify-reproducibility:
	@echo "[*] Verifying reproducible package build..."
	@TMP1=$$(mktemp -d) && TMP2=$$(mktemp -d) && \
	VERSION=$$(node -p 'require("./package.json").version') && \
	NEXUS_BUILD_CONTAINER_IMAGE=$(APPROVED_RUST_BUILD_IMAGE) bash scripts/package-linux.sh "v$$VERSION" "$$TMP1" && \
	NEXUS_BUILD_CONTAINER_IMAGE=$(APPROVED_RUST_BUILD_IMAGE) bash scripts/package-linux.sh "v$$VERSION" "$$TMP2" && \
	cmp "$$TMP1/nexus-linux-x86_64-v$$VERSION.tar.gz" "$$TMP2/nexus-linux-x86_64-v$$VERSION.tar.gz" && \
	cmp "$$TMP1/SHA256SUMS" "$$TMP2/SHA256SUMS" && \
	cmp "$$TMP1/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt" "$$TMP2/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt" && \
	cmp "$$TMP1/sbom.cdx.json" "$$TMP2/sbom.cdx.json" && \
	cmp "$$TMP1/install.sh" "$$TMP2/install.sh" && \
	rm -rf "$$TMP1" "$$TMP2"
	@echo "[+] Reproducible build verification succeeded (byte-identical artifacts)."

# `make test` runs every gate and fails at the end, so a CLI failure does not hide the terminal-scope or
# security result. It calls the two halves of `npm --prefix cli test` by name (test:cli, test:scope), so the
# step list lives only in cli/package.json.
# CI evaluator fixtures (tmpfs workspace and runtime root) come from `make test-ci`; see docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
test: test-fixture-notice
	@rc=0; \
	cargo test --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml || { echo "[!] FAILED: cargo test"; rc=1; }; \
	npm --prefix cli run test:cli || { echo "[!] FAILED: CLI suite"; rc=1; }; \
	npm --prefix cli run test:scope || { echo "[!] FAILED: terminal scope"; rc=1; }; \
	bash scripts/security_gates.sh || { echo "[!] FAILED: security gates"; rc=1; }; \
	if [ $$rc -ne 0 ]; then echo "[!] make test: one or more steps failed (all steps ran)"; fi; \
	exit $$rc

test-fixture-notice:
	@if [ -z "$$NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT" ] || [ -z "$$NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_RUNTIME_ROOT" ]; then \
	  echo "[i] NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT / NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_RUNTIME_ROOT are not set."; \
	  echo "[i] cli/test/eval_version_probe_storage.test.ts will FAIL without them, and cli/test/eval_integrity.test.ts"; \
	  echo "[i] runs its /dev/shm fallback branches instead of the capped-tmpfs ones. This is not a code defect."; \
	  echo "[i] Run 'make test-ci' to provision the same fixtures as CI (needs sudo)."; \
	fi

# Same gates as CI with the CI evaluator fixtures: mounts a capped tmpfs and runtime root, runs `make test`,
# then unmounts and removes only what it created. One-time host setup (not run here):
# scripts/install-evaluator-toolchains.sh, scripts/ensure-ci-bubblewrap.sh, scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh.
test-ci:
	+@if [ -n "$(findstring n,$(firstword -$(MAKEFLAGS)))" ]; then echo 'dry run: would run scripts/with-ci-fixtures.sh -- make test'; else bash scripts/with-ci-fixtures.sh -- $(MAKE) test; fi

| SI-6 | G-AI-3, G-AI-4 | CERI domain `semantic_integrity` with frozen scenarios (hidden invariant, self-validating implementation, compaction, conflicting specs, unauthorised acceptance edit, recovery, stale evidence, reviewer agreement, incomplete evidence) and cumulative-change scenarios | Scenarios run in CI; expected outcomes frozen outside implementation code | Additive |
| SI-7 | G-AI-5, G-AI-6 | Verify G-AI-6; add a kill-mid-tool-call fault-injection test; fix only what it shows | Test first; outcome decides whether code changes | Test-only unless a defect is shown |

| CG-3 structured diagnostics, evidence provenance, receipt dependencies | merged (#507) |
| DV-2 convergence signal | merged (#509) |
| SI-5 boundary rules, DV-3 regression obligations, DV-4 lineage and differential verification | deferred to v1.2.x |

```
  -> durable work units + dependencies (DurableOperationState, OperationStore)
  -> convergence scheduler (ConvergenceScheduler decides; OperationRunner owns time, execution, persistence)
  -> agent turn (AgentWorkUnitExecutor -> runTurn) / provider recovery (ProviderRecoveryController) / context admission
  -> tools + inference resources (ResourceRegistry, LocalLlmClient)
```

Interactive turns (REPL, TUI sidecar, `nexus run`) enter at "agent turn" directly; see section 8.

## 1. Execution-path matrix (baseline 9f103ee, before changes)

Read from the code, not from earlier reports. "Turn" = `AutonomousAgent.runTurn`, which owns `ProviderRecoveryController`,
`admitContext` (fail-closed capacity), truthful `TurnResult` and per-step durable checkpoints.

| Path (user-visible) | Work representation | Inference | Provider recovery | Context mgmt | Success determined by | Failure propagation | WAITING | BLOCKED | Durable recovery | Explicit deps | Resource eligibility | Truthful cancel | Restart/resume |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nexus run` / `ApplicationCore.runTask` | one turn (`agent.run`) | `runTurn` streaming | yes | yes (admission, compaction) | `TurnResult` execution/outcome | `TurnResult` → exit code / JSON | in-turn only (recovery wait) | turn `BLOCKED` (capacity) | task state per step | n/a | primary + failover endpoints | yes (signal) | `run -r <task>` |
| REPL turn (`repl.ts`) | one turn | `runTurn` | yes | yes | `TurnResult` | rendered | in-turn only | turn `BLOCKED` | task state | n/a | primary | yes (Ctrl-C) | `/recover` |
| Sidecar / TUI turn (`sidecar.ts`) | one turn | `runTurn` | yes | yes | `TurnResult` | turn events | in-turn only | turn `BLOCKED` | task state | n/a | primary | yes (signal) | recover command |
| `/tdd`, `run --tdd` | several turns (synthesizer) | `runTurn` | yes | yes | verifier evidence; last turn downgraded if TDD fails | `TurnResult` | in-turn only | turn `BLOCKED` | task state | implicit phase order | primary | yes (signal) | no |
| `nexus eval` | one turn per instance | `agent.run` | yes | yes | benchmark patch/test check | report | in-turn only | turn `BLOCKED` | task state | n/a | primary | no | no |

Contradictions found:

1. `/team` and `spawn_subagent` use a second agent loop (`runSubagent`) that bypasses provider recovery, the
   truthful `TurnResult`, cancellation and durability, and converts inference failure into a successful report.
2. Two "success" meanings: `TurnResult`/work-unit classification (evidence) vs `RoleTaskResult.success`
   ("the function returned").
3. Role → model routing exists twice: `/team` task-class headers vs scheduler requirements/resources.
4. Credential scope: `readLatestAuthToken` (stored aihost token) is attached to any endpoint without an explicit key
   (client constructor, 401 reload) and `buildConfig` bakes it into `config.apiKey`, which derived configs (planner,
   coder, subagents) then send to their own endpoints. Only the scheduler path was guarded (`noAmbientCredentials`).

## 2. The /team false success

Reproduction (`test/team_convergence.test.ts` tests 1–2, failing on 9f103ee): a provider that answers every chat
request with HTTP 400. `/team researcher …` returned `success: true` with the report
`Subagent failed during LLM inference: Inference error (HTTP 400) …`; `/team full …` ran all four roles on the
failed role's missing output and returned success.

Root cause: `TeamOrchestrator.executeRoleTask` built `{ success: true, output: await agent.runSubagent(...) }`, and
`runSubagent` caught inference failure and step-limit exhaustion and *returned* them as the report string. Success
meant "the function returned". `runFullWorkflow` passed each role's text to the next role unconditionally.

## 3. Lifecycle

One model for durable autonomous work, defined in `core/operation.ts` (header) and used by `nexus operation` and
`/team`:

# Nexus Code Architecture

Nexus Code utilizes a split architecture designed for performance, modularity, and security:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 TypeScript Orchestration Layer              │
│   • REPL / TUI Interface        • Agent Intelligence        │
│   • Skills Engine               • MCP JSON-RPC Client       │
│   • Plugin Lifecycle System     • Checkpoint & Undo Engine  │
│   • Secret Redactor             • Session Persistence       │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │ IPC / CLI Subprocess
┌──────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
│                    Rust Core Engine (ELF)                   │
│   • Path Resolution Jail        • Ripgrep Fast Search       │
│   • Atomic File Ops             • AST Symbol Parser         │
│   • Patch / Diff Applicator     • Tree & Metadata Inspector │
│   • POSIX Command Runner        • Destructive Command Guard │
└──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                               │ HTTP / SSE Gateway
┌──────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
│          OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint               │
│   • Local server: llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio, Ollama        │
│   • Optional gateway or cloud provider (operator-selected)  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 1. Rust Core Engine (`core/`)

The core engine is implemented in Rust 2024 edition and compiled into an optimized 64-bit ELF binary (`harness-core`).
- **`file_ops.rs`**: Safe reading with 8 MB cap and paging hints (`offset`, `length`), writing, atomic replacement, metadata inspection (`file_info`), batch reading (`batch_read` with 8 MB cap per entry), unified patch application (`patch_file`), and path traversal prevention (`resolve_safe_path`).
- **`search.rs`**: Fast ripgrep search using `ignore` and `grep` crates, regex symbol extraction across multi-language ASTs, and Unicode file tree formatting (`file_tree`).
- **`runner.rs`**: Child process execution and process ownership tracking via `ProcessRegistry`. Tracks process group IDs (`pgid`) mapped to request IDs. Implements `cancel` RPC (`SIGTERM` then `SIGKILL` after 2s), PTY `pgid` killing, shutdown sweeps on stdin EOF, `SIGTERM`, `SIGHUP` and `SIGINT` wi

---

## 2. TypeScript Orchestration Layer (`cli/`)

- **`AutonomousAgent` (`agent.ts`)**: Manages the iterative decision loop, token budgeting, prompt construction, and tool execution.
- **`InteractiveRepl` (`repl.ts`)**: Readline REPL with tab autocompletion, multiline input, direct shell escapes, and slash commands. Used when no terminal is attached, or with `nexus repl`.
- **`SidecarServer` (`sidecar.ts`)**: Runs the agent for the Rust live TUI (`core/src/bin/nexus_tui`), speaking NDJSON over stdio. The TUI owns all keyboard input, including approval input safety.
- **`LocalLlmClient` (`client.ts`)**: Streaming SSE OpenAI-compatible client with automatic auth token discovery and token rotation retry.
- **`CheckpointManager` (`checkpoint.ts`)**: Creates safe git and tree checkpoints before every turn and manages workspace rollbacks (`/undo`).
- **`McpClientManager` (`mcp.ts`)**: Stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 client connecting external MCP servers from `~/.config/nexus/mcp.json`.
- **`SkillManager` (`skills.ts`)**: Auto-discovers and dynamically loads `SKILL.md` documents on-demand.
- **`PluginManager` (`plugins.ts`)**: Lifecycle hook manager supporting `onTurnStart`, `onToolCall`, `onToolResult`, and custom tool registration.
- **`TerminalUI` (`ui.ts`)**: Formatted terminal output with live spinners, colored diffs, milestone plans, and secret scrubber.

---

## 3. Controls and their limits

Each control below is stated with what it does **not** cover. The v1.0.0 plan (`docs/v1.0.0/`) tracks the open gaps.

1. **Workspace path jail (file tools).** The Rust file tools (read, write, edit, delete, list, search) canonicalize every path against the workspace root and reject `..`, absolute paths and symlink escapes, rechecking the opened descriptor. *Limit:* for `run_command`, path protection is advisory. Ho
2. **Destructive-command tripwire.** Shell-words tokenization in TypeScript (`cli/src/security.ts`) and Rust (`core/src/runner.rs`) stops obviously destructive commands (`rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, raw block device writes, fork bombs) without false positives on legitimate project commands (`rm -rf ./build`,
3. **Approvals and posture defaults.** Per amended DEC-01, unset permission mode defaults to `review` regardless of folder trust. `--mode auto` permits writes and commands while retaining first-use egress approval per origin; `--yes` and `NEXUS_APPROVAL_MODE=auto` enable full access and bypass appro
4. **Workspace trust.** Trust is managed via `nexus trust` and stored in `~/.config/nexus/trusted_workspaces.json`; interactive startup asks for trust before loading project instructions (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEX.md`, `.nexusrules`). In untrusted workspaces, project instructions, workspace M
5. **Secret redaction.** Terminal output, audit logs and durable state pass through pattern-based scrubbers, and outbound content is classified and tokenized. *Limit:* it is pattern-based, so secrets with no recognizable shape are not detected.
6. **Container sandbox and argv isolation.** `--sandbox` confines execution using Linux Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) or Docker. The sandbox argv is constructed as a direct array without shell wrapping (REQ-SEC-109), preventing shell escaping flaws on complex workspace paths. The write-mode `bwrap` sandbox (
   - *Filesystem:* the host root is bound read-only (`--ro-bind / /`, remounted read-only) with a fresh `/dev`, `/proc` and an empty `/tmp`; the workspace is bound writable. `$HOME` is replaced by an empty tmpfs, so `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.config/nexus` and browser profiles do not exist 
   - *Environment:* `--clearenv`, then only the scrubbed command environment (`cli/src/command_env.ts`) is set. Variables that came from `~/.config/nexus/config.env`, names that look like credentials (`*_API_KEY`, `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET`, `*_PASSWORD`, `AWS_*`, `GH_TOKEN`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, ...) and pr
   - *Network:* off by default (`--unshare-net`; Docker `--network none`). The operator opts in with `--sandbox-network` or `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK=1` in the operator environment. `--yes` does not enable it. `--sandbox-network` without `--sandbox` has no effect and warns. `--read-only` mode is always
   - *Process isolation:* `--unshare-pid` with a fresh `/proc` (host processes and their `/proc/<pid>/environ` are invisible) and `--die-with-parent` (every descendant dies with the runner). These flags are on both the write-mode and the read-only `bwrap` branches. `--new-session` is deliberately no
   - *Docker:* the image is pinned by digest in one constant, `DOCKER_SANDBOX_IMAGE` (`alpine:3.23@sha256:469c9ea4...`). The operator may substitute another with `NEXUS_SANDBOX_DOCKER_IMAGE` (operator environment or `config.env`); it must match `name@sha256:<64 hex>`, otherwise no container is start
   - In `--read-only` mode, `$HOME` is mounted as `--tmpfs $HOME` and the host root is not exposed (REQ-SEC-104); without bwrap, strict path confinement rejects paths outside the workspace.

   *Limits, stated plainly:* (a) **Without `--sandbox`** a command runs as the same user as Nexus. The scrubbed environment keeps credentials out of what the command inherits (`env`, `printenv`), but the command can still read the operator's files (for example `~/.config/nexus/config.env`, `~/.ssh`)
7. **Process group lifecycle and residual setsid escape risk.** The runner registers child process groups at spawn and terminates entire groups (`killpg`) on turn cancel, client crash, or process shutdown (REQ-AGT-109, REQ-SEC-106). Background services explicitly registered survive turn cancel but a

## Compaction and continuity

Long-task continuity (no step ceiling, state-aware repetition, objective-scoped execution tracking), the durable
compaction commit, queued operator `/compact`, and optional provider capabilities with labelled token accounting are
described in `docs/COMPACTION_AND_CONTINUITY.md`.

content.content:
## 8. Single-agent boundary

An interactive turn stays a direct `runTurn`: one turn whose `TurnResult` is the outcome, with provider recovery
and context admission inside it. Wrapping it in an operation would add a store and lock but no new truth. Work that
has dependencies, must outlive a resource becoming unavailable, may wait, or must resume after a restart is an
operation. `spawn_subagent` is in-turn delegation: its result is a tool result of the parent's durable turn and is
now truthful (`SubagentResult.completed`; the tool reports `success: false` when the child did not complete). The
child is complete only by `turnSucceeded` on its own turn: its `task_completed` goes through the same receipt
validation as any turn (a rejected receipt keeps it working), and a plain-text report over unverified changes is
not completion. The child's workspace changes count as the parent's, so the parent must verify them before it can
complete; it cannot finish as `NOT_REQUIRED`.

## 9. Restart and reboot

Process restart: proven. Operation state and each unit's task conversation are durable; a driver killed at any
point leaves a lock whose pid is dead, which the next `nexus operation resume` takes over; interrupted RUNNING units
are reconciled (bounded unknown-outcome resumes).

Host reboot: Nexus has no daemon or service lifecycle (the only long-lived child is the per-process Rust RPC
helper), so none was added. After a reboot the state is intact and a lock written before boot is treated as stale
even if its pid number has been reused (`OperationStore.acquire` compares the lock time with boot time). The
smallest integration point is an OS boot hook that runs `nexus operation resume` (with no id it resumes the latest
WAITING or RUNNING operation for the workspace; BLOCKED operations are excluded because they need a decision), e.g.
a user systemd unit or `@reboot` cron entry. That hook is not installed by Nexus.

## 10. Remaining duplication and limitations

- `runSubagent` remains a second, in-turn agent loop for `spawn_subagent`. It now has provider recovery, context
  admission with `measureAdmission` (closing the strict token counting gap per REQ-AGT-111 / AGT-05), matched
  offered and accepted tool sets via `getEffectiveTools()`, token accounting merged into parent stats, and a truthful result.
  Remaining divergences from `runTurn` deferred to post-v1 include: non-streaming responses, in-turn subagents are non-durable
  (no task state records on disk per REQ-AGT-105), no empty-reply retry, no backoff for poll loops, no operator steering queue,
  and no cancellation signal separate from the parent turn. Folding it into a single shared step function remains post-v1.
- The legacy REPL and the slash router each wire `/team` to `TeamOrchestrator` (display only; same operation).
- Roles run sequentially; the scheduler would allow parallel units but no concurrency was added.
- Re-verified for v1.2.1 (PC-2): an exhausted 502/504 parks the unit and it resumes (I3); an unknown host (ENOTFOUND) is
  configuration, so it blocks with an operator decision by design; parked advisory work no longer postpones the decision
  a blocked required unit needs (I4, fixed); the operation lock takeover is serialised and an unreadable lock goes stale
  after 30 s on the same host and filesystem clock (fixed; stale takeover needs `/usr/bin/flock` and fails closed without it). Still open: a context-capacity block does not reroute to a larger qualified resource.
- Resource requirements per role are qualification labels; real capability metadata depends on provider catalogs
  (`--discover`), which aihost aliases do not publish beyond the model list.

# Evaluation harness (qualification assessment §9)

`run.mjs` runs tasks against one agent configuration and appends a JSON line per run; `score.mjs` reports the scores
separately (never combined), per task and configuration, with 95 % Wilson intervals.

`docs/v1.0.0/READINESS.md` is a historical checkpoint at source revision `6151a23`; use this file and the current
runner source for evaluator behavior added after that revision. Neither document represents completed M5 qualification.

```bash
node eval/run.mjs --config eval/configs/gateway-engineering-deep.json --out eval/out/<label> [--only id,id] [--runs N]
node eval/score.mjs eval/out/<label>/results.jsonl          # markdown table; --json for machine output
node eval/score.mjs --pairs "$NEXUS_RESULTS" "$GOOSE_RESULTS" "$OPENCODE_RESULTS"
```

## Installed versioned datasets

Installed releases expose the versioned runner through the Nexus CLI:

```bash
nexus eval --dataset /path/to/core-v1 --split benchmark --runs 1 \
  --isolated-home --output ./results/benchmark.json
```

The dataset path must be a versioned dataset directory. The installed command loads its runner from the package named by

Audit of worktree `/home/mike/nexus-wt/invariants` at 65c76b28. Paths below are under `cli/src` unless noted. Nothing was edited or run.

## 1. Review, planning and acceptance behaviour

**(a) Planner and objective extraction**
- There is no LLM planner or requirement extractor. `core/objective.ts:242` (`seedRequirements`) regex-splits numbered items (`1.`, `R3:`) from the objective. Fewer than two items becomes a single requirement R1. [VERIFIED]
- `core/objective.ts:34` defines `RequirementKind = "feature" | "constraint" | "invariant"`, and `typedItem` (:265) reads only an operator-written `Invariant:` or `Constraint:` prefix, optionally ending `[verify: cmd]`. This is the only invariant-aware mechanism. [PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED]
- Hard requirements are gated (:48): "Constraints and invariants hold for the whole task; unlike a feature they are not done on the model's word." Features are still marked `implemented` on the model's word.
- Unnumbered or prose invariants are not captured.
- `/team` copies the raw objective into every role's prompt (`team.ts:47-58`). It sets no `authorizedScope` and no kind. `taskClass` is only a gateway routing header (`client.ts:960`, `X-Task-Class`), not risk classification. [VERIFIED]
- `agent.ts:1258` "planner"/"coder" are model tiers, not requirement planning.

**(b) Implementer prompt** (`agent.ts:4677-4723`)
- Operating rules cover explore first, "PRECISE EDITS & PATCHES", "VERIFICATION", "AUTONOMOUS COMPLETION", and "Use `update_plan` only for work with three or more distinct phases".
- The agent identity line says it "solve[s] coding problems, build[s] features, fix[es] bugs, and refactor[s] codebases".
- Role addendum (`core/roles.ts:~60`): "Make minimal, surgical edits using edit_file and patch_file. Verify syntactical correctness and avoid unintended breaking changes." The architect addendum says "design clean, modular solutions adhering to existing codebase idioms."
- There is no text on scope discipline, avoiding unnecessary abstraction, preserving invariants, or behaviour changes hidden in a refactor.
- `fewshots.ts` holds tool-call exemplars only. `harness_notes.ts` is message provenance, not guidance. `AGENTS.md` ("Preserve existing comments and unrelated changes") is loaded as project rules only in trusted workspaces. [VERIFIED_ARCHITECTURAL_DEBT]
- The TDD block (`agent.ts:~4692`) has a "REFACTOR" phase that means "run the full suite".

**(c) Independent review** (`core/independent_review.ts`)
- The prompt (:283-330) instructs: "3. Check for regressions, unhandled edge cases, security boundaries, and incomplete logic." and "4. unprovenCriteria … Any entry makes the verdict REJECT".
- The verdict schema (:36-43) is `verdict, verifiedObservations, suspectedDefects[{path,line,description}], unprovenCriteria, scopeViolations, reviewerConfidenceNote`. [VERIFIED]
- There is no field or criterion for coupling, hidden side effects, abstraction justification, rationale preservation, behaviour change inside a refactor, or change cost. [VERIFIED_ARCHITECTURAL_DEBT]
- `unresolvedAssumptions` is accepted and stored (:32, :236, :250) but never rendered into the prompt, so it is a dead field. [VERIFIED_DEFECT, minor]
- The `acceptance_reviewer` escalation criteria (`core/specialist_profiles.ts:141`) are "lack unambiguous deterministic test proofs" and "touches files outside authorized change boundary". Both cover proof and scope only.

**(d) Acceptance**
- The turn verdict is `EngineeringOutcome` (`core/turn.ts:26`): VERIFIED, REGRESSION_FREE, UNVERIFIED, NOT_REQUIRED and so on.
- `task_completed` (`agent.ts:~4745`) gates on open and blocked requirements, then on the verifier. With no discoverable verifier, completion is allowed but UNVERIFIED (exit code 2).

**Risk classification**
- None by task kind (correctness repair, refactor, cosmetic). The eval harness has `tier`/`class` metadata only, and `eval/tasks/t2-refactor-tax` is a refactor task whose hidden test greps for `ROUND_HALF_UP|quantize`. [VERIFIED]

**Scope violation detection**
- `detectScopeViolations` (`core/independent_review.ts:201`) compares the diff's file paths to a prefix list, with `"*"` meaning all. It runs in the prompt (as `[AUTOMATED SCOPE WARNING]`) and in the verdict parser, where any violation forces REJECT (:409).
- `authorizedScope` is operator-declared per unit (`core/operation.ts:462`, `normalizeScope`) and passed at `operation_runner_execution.ts:750`. With none declared, no scope claim is made.
- It is a post-hoc, file-path-only check at review time. There is no write-time enforcement, no derivation from the plan, and no `/team` default. [PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED]

**Can "cleaner code" substitute for verifier evidence?**
- No. `parseIndependentReviewVerdict` (:401-407) forces REJECT when `verifierExitCode === undefined` or non-zero. The runner derives that exit code from a dependency's `PASSED && hasExecutedTests` (`operation_runner_execution.ts:~765`). A reviewer ACCEPT cannot stand alone. [ALREADY_ADDRESSED]
- Conversely, a passing verifier plus ACCEPT suffices, and nothing evaluates refactor justification. [VERIFIED_ARCHITECTURAL_DEBT]
- Related debt: the truncation gate `if (pkg.unifiedDiff.length > 20000 && pkg.verifierExitCode !== 0)` (:412) is unreachable as a decider, because earlier branches already reject whenever the exit code is not 0. A diff over 20000 characters with a passing verifier can therefore be ACCEPTed after the reviewer saw only the first 20000 characters. The literal `20000` is duplicated at :283, :287 and :412.

## 2. Rationale preservation

**Mechanisms that exist**
- ADRs and decision logs: `docs/DEC01_*.md`, `docs/DEC02_*.md`, `docs/v1.0.0/DECISIONS.md` (DEC-01..20), `docs/v1.1.0/DECISIONS.md` (DEC-V11-xx).
- Code comments citing IDs: about 75 `REQ-*` and 17 `DEC-*` in src, for example `tokens.ts:26` ("DEC-17: …"). DEC-17 exists in `docs/v1.0.0/DECISIONS.md`.
- Test names carry IDs (about 144 `ACC-*` and 124 `REQ-*` in `cli/test`).
- There are zero `WHY` markers.

**Enforcement of doc/code consistency**
- `scripts/check_requirements.mjs` runs in CI. It checks that each requirement row links a spec, a plan and an ACC id, and that each `test:<file>::"<name>"` reference exists in a real test file. It never scans `cli/src` or `core/src`, so the code-to-rationale direction is unchecked. [VERIFIED]
- Other doc/code checks in CI: `sync-version.mjs --check`, `check_doc_versions.mjs`, `check_deprecated_lock.mjs`, `cli/test/eval_single_source.test.ts` (core-v1 generated from `eval/tasks`), and the pinned `semantic_integrity.scenarios.sha256`.
- `cli/scripts/check_test_leaks.mjs` is a shrink-only baseline ratchet over test sources. It is a usable precedent for a locality ratchet.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` is `* @mikeholownych` plus `/scripts/`, `/.github/`, `/docs/releases/` and the CERI fixtures. It has no rationale-based protection of `cli/src/core`. [VERIFIED]
- `ci.yml` has no lint, dependency-boundary or doc-link check. The PR template asks to "link requirement IDs where applicable", but it is manual.

**Guards whose rationale is only in a comment or nowhere**
